declared.name: Agent cap
declared.description: A configurable cap on how many headless Claude sessions and builds run at once on the VPS (agent-slots@1, framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs). Extras wait in a queue (FIFO within boss / urgent / normal / low) and start by themselves when a slot frees and memory allows; finished sessions don't count and close by themselves (logs kept). Settings (hot-reloaded): max running agents, max heavy test/build steps at once, memory guard, close-after, priority rules; shown in Settings → Plugins → Agent cap and in the Breakroom (Agent swarm) settings. Slots used / cap in the activity banner's summary, the queue (position, waiting since, Move up, Cancel) on the Builds page, 'waiting for a desk' on swarm agents past the cap, and a systems-check item when the memory guard trips often or swap stays in use. VPS hard build limit (build-limit@1): the host refuses the N+1st headless build whatever the queue thinks (default 8, one config file), runs every build in axf-builds.slice (CPUQuota, MemoryMax) and caps docker test containers; live usage on the settings tab, banner chip and queue title; only Brett's signed-in console changes it.

declared.name: Agent swarm

Agent jobs: recurring job types (job-type@1) owned by hired agents, routed by framework/cli/agent-job.mjs (owner, duty, budget, brief, headless launch, run on the agent). Breakroom: agent cards and profiles, a Jobs view, statuses, salaries, discipline and a group chat with a vibe-ceiling settings suite. Section owners (crew-sections@1): every section that acts on its own has one employee who posts its key events in the group chat (framework/cli/crew-say.mjs), reassigned in the settings tab.

declared.name: Follow Amber
declared.description: One switch: Follow Amber. On: whenever Amber (any Claude session through the console's MCP or axHub) mentions a console screen, settings tab, dialog or anything that needs you, she calls console_show and the console opens it right away, focused and highlighted, with what she said as a note; and every axHub held or confirm call for you pops up in the console as an approval dialog (title, plain description, the exact call folded away, the countdown on veto calls, big Approve and Deny that act on one tap, a queue when there are several). Decisions stay in the console: a tap goes to axHub through the approvals banner's relay with your own signed-in hub session, and the result shows in the pop-up; the console never approves anything by itself. Off: nothing opens by itself and approvals stay in the approvals banner. Switch it in Settings → Plugins → Follow Amber, the right-click menu anywhere in the console, or the banner chip. Showing only navigates (it runs with the navigate permission alone), so it never waits on a veto. REST /api/plugins/follow-amber (state, show, approval, stream), MCP console_show and console_follow, CLI axf follow-amber <command>.

declared.name: GitHub
declared.description: One-click GitHub App for the whole stack (github-app@1): Settings → Plugins → GitHub makes a private GitHub App on MossesX through GitHub's manifest flow (Create → Install on All repositories → Authorize as Brett). The console then mints its own installation tokens from the app's key (1 h, renewed at 50 min: they never die for good) and keeps GITHUB_TOKEN on them, so git, gh, the push banner, CI reads and the activity feed use the app; the old personal token stays as the fallback. A user token from the same app (refreshed by itself) creates repos. Health items for the app key, installation, token, rate limit and user token. Keys and tokens stay on the console server (.axf-console/github-app, 0700/0600) and never reach a browser; the broker is framework/cli/github-token.mjs.

declared.name: Push banner
declared.description: A banner listing every branch that isn't on main yet in AmberX-AXF and axHub (commits ahead/behind, age, last commit, its open PR and that PR's CI), with Open PR and Merge: every change reaches main only through its PR (one is opened for every branch), brought up to date with main and re-tested before it merges (not behind, CI passed on the pinned head; re-checked on the server). Auto-merge takes ready PRs oldest first, one merge per round, and sets branch protection on main where the token may. Auto-land (land/land.mjs, plain scripts on the VPS, no model calls) lands every finished build: worktree cleaned, main merged in with the builds files newer-wins, PR opened, CI started, merged here in dependency order once green and not held by UI Review; blocked builds are pushed to Brett once, in plain words. The console server talks to GitHub with its own token, which never reaches the browser. Merge queue (0.7.0): GitHub's own merge queue needs an organisation-owned repo, so the queue is ours: ready PRs line up, each is tested once on top of main + every PR ahead of it (queue/pr-<n> branches), the green head merges with no retest, a red one is kicked out with the reason in plain words and the ones behind it are retested without it; CI runs only what a change touches, PRs run light checks while the queue is on. Merge queue view, banner chip, REST + MCP + CLI. 0.7.1 (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "Stop merging these things one at a time"): auto-land is off by default and only the merge queue merges AmberX-AXF; GitHub reads are cached with ETags (a 304 costs no API call) and held back when the shared limit runs low; the console redeploys once per stack. 0.8.0 (Nov 10 2026, Brett: "Everything needs to go into the merge queue so we can make one build out of it before we send it to CI"): batch mode by default: every finished build gets a PR and joins the queue, up to batchSize ready PRs are combined into one commit on queue/batch, CI runs once, and a green batch lands on main as that one commit (one redeploy); a red batch is split in half until the PR that broke it is kicked out. Merge on AmberX-AXF puts the PR in the queue.
